evidence.title: May7 minutes in the October agenda record15 of931 responding federal judges encountering deepfake challenges, with45% response.
evidence.observation: May7 minutes in the October agenda record15 of931 responding federal judges encountering deepfake challenges, with45% response. Challenge frequency is not fabricated-evidence prevalence. Draft901(c) would require an evidential trigger before heightened authentication; it is a proposal, not enacted law.

source_locations.SRC-103: May7 meeting minutes, PDF pages 12 and19; draft901(c), PDF page 149

evidence.limitations: Agenda is not October15 meeting minutes. Survey summarized in May7 minutes: response bias, self-report and undetected fabrication remain. No individual case independently checked. Committee members disagreed whether existing authentication rules suffice. Low observed challenge rates neither establish a crisis nor rule out undetected fabrication.

terms.name: Evidence laundering through AI
terms.definition: The appearance of credibility or corroboration acquired by low-integrity material when AI systems retrieve, summarize, cite, or re-present it. Multiple apparently agreeing outputs may share the same original, manipulated source.

terms.name: Investigative indicator
terms.definition: An observed characteristic or combination of signals that provides a reason to investigate a possible event, mechanism, or hidden relationship without establishing that it occurred.

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.
